country_overview: Brazil operates a floating exchange rate regime administered by the Central Bank of Brazil (Banco Central do Brasil - BCB). The Brazilian Real is subject to certain capital controls and reporting requirements, while current account transactions are largely liberalised.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in foreign currency without limit but must declare amounts of USD 10,000 or equivalent. Export of foreign currency is restricted and subject to BCB rules.
summary.business: Businesses must route significant foreign exchange transactions through authorised banks. Capital repatriation and certain payments require BCB approval or documentation.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Foreign currency may be brought into Brazil without limit. Amounts of USD 10,000 or equivalent must be declared to Brazilian Customs upon arrival.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Foreign currency may be taken out up to the amount declared on entry or supported by authorised bank documentation. Residents are subject to BCB limits.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: USD 10,000 or equivalent in foreign currency or negotiable instruments at entry and exit. Declaration to Brazilian Customs is mandatory.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Brazilian residents are subject to BCB limits and approval requirements when holding or using foreign currency accounts. General unrestricted access requires specific authorisation.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds more freely through authorised banks.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border business transactions must be settled through authorised banks in accordance with BCB foreign exchange regulations.
rules.exchange_controls: Brazil maintains a floating exchange regime with controls on certain capital account transactions. Current account transactions are largely liberalised.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion is available through authorised banks and licensed exchange offices. Documentation is required for large transactions.
